key_insight: FrozenLGP makes divide-and-conquer QAOA work on dense or highly connected graphs by freezing a minimal set of obstructing vertices and absorbing their effects into the remaining Ising model.
engineering_relevance: This turns graph partitionability from a structural assumption into an adaptive preprocessing step, enabling distributed quantum optimization on larger and more realistic near-term hardware workloads.
method: Use a max-flow/min-vertex-cut routine to find the smallest set of vertices blocking a partition.
Classically fix those vertices' spin assignments and preserve their contributions as linear bias terms on neighboring active qubits.
Proceed with standard divide-and-conquer QAOA on the reduced, now-partitionable graph.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 100% decomposition coverage up to 10,000 vertices, versus 4.6% for the standard baseline on high-connectivity graphs, while maintaining MaxCut quality and improving noise robustness.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable classical cut finding and spin-freezing choices, so its runtime overhead and sensitivity to graph structure should be validated on real hardware pipelines.
paper_title: Adaptive Qubit Freezing Enables Robust Graph Partitioning for Divide-and-Conquer QAOA
